output.brief:
The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14. It started on 3 March at 10:41 UTC, when Corvane's automatic rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17). The rule blocks password logins that use the nettle-http library, which every Android version uses. It blocked about 41,300 installs, and 92% of them had logged in successfully in the prior 90 days. They are real customers, not bots. The drop is the same on every app version and OS version, with or without the March patch. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. A rollback of 6.14 would not help, and it would affect only the 5–10% of users already on that release.

What to do next: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password-login path, keeping all other protections active. Then confirm in telemetry that Android password success returns to about 96%. Don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Both would worsen the lockout or hide it. I'm fairly confident, around 90%. The call-volume link to this drop is plausible but unproven, because the call reason codes are unreliable.
